chapters.title: Anatomy of a Loop
chapters.caption: Trigger, action, stop condition — goal, verification, and what 'done' objectively means.

chapters.title: When You Need a Loop
chapters.caption: Most tasks don't need loops; use one when work repeats and AI can check what done means.

chapters.title: Loop Structures
chapters.caption: Solo loops, major + checker, and manager loops that orchestrate subagents.

chapters.title: Five Loop Patterns
chapters.caption: Stateless, self-learning, multi-agent, verification, and workflow-improvement loops.

chapters.title: Retrospectives & Matching
chapters.caption: End every loop by asking how to improve it; match the pattern to the task's shape.

chapters.title: Stateless & Skill Examples
chapters.caption: Get every test passing with a Haiku checker; a reusable skill that improves each run.

chapters.title: Four-Reviewer Multi-Agent
chapters.caption: One orchestrator, four persona lenses reviewing the same work across multiple rounds.

chapters.title: Super Loops
chapters.caption: A manager loop spawning worker loops with shared memory handoffs between subagents.

chapters.title: Parallelism & Isolation
chapters.caption: Fold time by running scoped worker loops in parallel, each isolated to its own scope.

chapters.title: Five-Part Prompt Formula
chapters.caption: Goal, done-when, tools, verify, unveil — the prompt skeleton for every loop.

chapters.title: Stop-Condition Pitfalls
chapters.caption: 'Until satisfied' burns infinite tokens; visual checks — does the 3D plane actually render?

chapters.title: Eight Reliability Rules
chapters.caption: Checkable goals, separate checkers, logging, memory, hard stops — and the 8.5M-token cautionary tale.

chapters.title: Token-Efficiency Tips
chapters.caption: Summarize context, Headroom compression, caching, memory hygiene, clean agent handoffs.

chapters.title: Q&A: Harness & Hygiene
chapters.caption: Waves, creative use cases, goal discipline, and observing many loops at once.

chapters.title: Introduction to Agents
chapters.caption: The speaker begins by reflecting on a past project involving 700 agents, emphasizing the value of iterative learning despite unexpected duration.

chapters.title: Model Orchestration
chapters.caption: He explains his system of using multiple models like Haiku, One, and LightLM, routing tasks based on specific needs and delegating to specialized models.

chapters.title: Automated Validation
chapters.caption: The speaker describes a process where multiple models act as validators, simulating a consortium to judge outputs and improve over time.

chapters.title: Iterative Learning
chapters.caption: He highlights the importance of self-learning loops, prompting variations, and refining processes based on what works across iterations.

chapters.title: Data Serialization
chapters.caption: The speaker outlines his approach to logging and storing data using vector databases and .md files for redundancy and traceability.

chapters.title: Task Management
chapters.caption: He recommends using tools like Notion or Asana with open tickets and memory IDs to preserve context across long-term projects.

chapters.title: Personal Motivation
chapters.caption: The speaker shares that this talk is tied to his upcoming birthday and a personal challenge to grow through discomfort.

chapters.title: QR Code & Connection
chapters.caption: He presents a QR code linking to his website, offering contact options and a discount, encouraging audience engagement.

chapters.title: Closing Remarks
chapters.caption: The speaker thanks the audience and previews the next day’s session, emphasizing deep dives into tokenization, observability, and agent systems.

chapters.title: Networking Call
chapters.caption: He invites attendees to network, reiterates the next day’s schedule, and reminds them to clean up after themselves before leaving.
